payload.title: Add secure login to this application.

contract.goal: Implement secure login endpoints for this application, reusing the existing user model and session store
constraints: Reuse the existing SessionStore and UserRepo; do not add a database
Do not add new paid infrastructure or external services
Keep all changes covered by vitest tests under tests/auth/

acceptance_criteria.condition: A valid login credential creates a user session and GET /me returns the user
An expired login credential is rejected with HTTP 401
A login credential cannot be reused after its first successful use
Changes stay within the allowed scope
The whole test suite still passes

contract.goal: Add a minimal login page that submits an email address to the backend login endpoint and shows the result
constraints: Plain HTML and vanilla JavaScript only; no framework, no build step; create the public/ directory if it does not exist
The page must call POST /auth/request with a JSON body {"email": "..."} and display the response message

acceptance_criteria.condition: public/login.html exists and contains a form posting an email to /auth/request
Changes stay within the allowed scope

questions.text: What response shape must the page display after POST /auth/request? Options: (A) parse JSON and display its `message` field for both success and error responses; (B) display the raw response text; (C) accept either by parsing JSON when possible and falling back to text. Please also specify the expected behavior for network failures if it differs from showing a readable error message.

Which login mechanism? The User model has no password field and src/email/stub.ts is listed as an input, and the acceptance criteria describe an expiring, single-use 'login credential'. Options: (a) email magic link: POST an email, a one-time token is sent via EmailSender and later exchanged for a session; (b) email one-time code (short numeric code sent by email, entered back); (c) email + password (would require adding a password hash to the seeded users, which conflicts with 'reuse the existing user model'); (d) something else.

Endpoint names and payload shapes? Proposal for the magic-link case: POST /auth/login with JSON {"email"} returning 202 {"status":"sent"} and sending an email whose text contains the token; POST /auth/verify with JSON {"token"} (or GET /auth/verify?token=...) creating the session and returning 200 with the user; GET /me returning the user when authenticated. Accept the proposal, or specify different paths / payloads / response bodies.

How should the session reach the client after login? Options: (a) HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax cookie named e.g. 'session' set on verify and read by GET /me; (b) session id returned in the JSON body and sent back as 'Authorization: Bearer <id>'; (c) both.
Lifetimes? Proposed defaults: login token expires after 15 minutes, session expires after 24 hours, both injectable via a clock for tests. Confirm or give other values.

Behaviour when the login email does not match any user? Options: (a) respond exactly as for a known user (202, no email sent) to prevent account enumeration; (b) respond 404 {"error":"user not found"} like GET /users/:id does. Default if unanswered: (a).

Error responses for rejected tokens? Proposed: 401 {"error":"invalid or expired login token"} for unknown, expired and already-used tokens alike; 400 for malformed request bodies. Also: should a POST /auth/logout endpoint that revokes the current session be included (default: yes, it is small and reuses SessionStore.revoke)?

answers.answer: (a) email magic link: POST an email, a one-time token is sent via the existing EmailSender, later exchanged for a session.

Use these exact endpoints so the frontend task can match them: POST /auth/request with JSON {"email"} -> 202 {"status":"sent","message":"Check your email for a login link"} and send the token by email; POST /auth/verify with JSON {"token"} -> 200 with the user object; GET /me -> the user when authenticated. No /auth/login path.
(a) HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax cookie named session, set on /auth/verify and read by GET /me.
Confirmed: login token expires after 15 minutes, session after 24 hours, both injectable via a clock.
(a) respond exactly as for a known user (202, no email sent) to prevent account enumeration.
Confirmed: 401 {"error":"invalid or expired login token"} for unknown, expired and already-used tokens; 400 for malformed bodies; include POST /auth/logout.

interpretation: Create a standalone public/login.html page using only HTML, basic CSS, and vanilla JavaScript.
Submit the entered email with fetch as POST /auth/request using Content-Type application/json and the exact JSON shape {"email":"..."}.
Render the backend message in the page, preferring a parsed JSON message field and falling back to raw response text; render a readable message for network failures.
assumptions: Browser-native email validation and a required field are sufficient client-side validation.
The same result region may display successful responses, backend error responses, and network errors.
No backend or server-routing changes are needed because /auth/request already exists.
risks: A malformed JSON response without a message field requires the raw response body fallback.
The command criterion verifies static markers, so an additional local behavioral check will be used to validate the JavaScript logic.

verification_plan.AC-1: Run the exact contract command, then inspect/test the page script to confirm the submit handler sends POST /auth/request with JSON and renders JSON-message, text fallback, and network-error outcomes.
verification_plan.AC-2: Run git status and git diff --name-only and confirm every changed path matches public/** or tests/ui/**.

payload.message: Contract v2 accepted; beginning scoped inspection and implementation.

interpretation: Add an email magic-link login: POST /auth/request takes {email}, always answers 202 {status:'sent', message:'Check your email for a login link'}, and only when the email matches a UserRepo user does it mint a random single-use token (15 min TTL) and send it through the existing EmailSender.

POST /auth/verify takes {token}; a live, unused token is consumed (deleted), a 24h session is created in the existing SessionStore, an HttpOnly SameSite=Lax cookie named 'session' is set, and the user object is returned with 200. Unknown, expired or already-used tokens get 401 {error:'invalid or expired login token'}; malformed bodies get 400.

GET /me reads the 'session' cookie, looks it up in SessionStore and returns the user with 200, or keeps the existing 401 {error:'not authenticated'} response. POST /auth/logout revokes the cookie's session and clears the cookie.

Login tokens live in a new in-memory store under src/auth/ with an injectable clock; createApp gains optional injectable dependencies (users, sessions, email sender, clock) so tests stay hermetic. No database, no new services, no frontend changes.
All new behaviour is covered by vitest tests under tests/auth/, including the two files the acceptance checks name.
assumptions: The email body will contain the raw token on its own line (plus a relative /auth/verify hint) so a frontend or test can extract it; the exact wording is not contractually fixed.
Tokens are generated with crypto.getRandomValues / randomBytes (32 bytes, base64url) and stored only in memory, keyed by token, so they are lost on restart, which is acceptable for this demo.
The cookie is not marked Secure because the demo runs over plain HTTP on localhost; the attribute can be enabled later without changing the API.
Existing callers of createApp(users?) keep working: the first parameter stays a UserRepo or becomes an options object, and existing tests in tests/ are left untouched.
risks: The seeded 401 response for GET /me is asserted by tests/app.test.ts; I must keep that exact body for the unauthenticated case.
AC-3 (no token reuse) is verified by human review, so I will also add an explicit vitest case for it under tests/auth/ to make the evidence concrete.
Cookie parsing in Hono requires hono/cookie helpers; if the pinned hono version behaves differently I will fall back to manual header parsing.

verification_plan.AC-1: tests/auth/valid-login.test.ts: request a link for a seeded user, extract the token from the MemoryEmailSender, POST /auth/verify, assert 200 with the user and a Set-Cookie 'session' header, then GET /me with that cookie and assert 200 with the same user. Run npx vitest run tests/auth/valid-login.test.ts and confirm it passes.
verification_plan.AC-2: tests/auth/expired-login.test.ts: inject a mutable clock, request a token, advance the clock past 15 minutes, POST /auth/verify and assert 401 {error:'invalid or expired login token'} and no session cookie. Run npx vitest run tests/auth/expired-login.test.ts and confirm it passes.
verification_plan.AC-3: tests/auth/token-reuse.test.ts: verify a token successfully once, then POST /auth/verify again with the same token and assert 401 and no new session cookie; also inspect the implementation to confirm the token is deleted on first successful use before the session is created.
verification_plan.AC-4: Run git status / git diff --name-only before submitting and confirm every changed path is under src/auth/**, src/app.ts or tests/auth/**.
verification_plan.AC-5: Run npx vitest run (whole suite) and npx tsc --noEmit and confirm both exit 0.

payload.message: Contract v2 accepted; starting with failing tests under tests/auth/ (TDD), then src/auth/ implementation and app wiring.
UI tests written within tests/ui for email input, JSON submission, response display, and network-error behavior.
Implementation complete: public/login.html now submits the required JSON request and displays JSON, text, or network-error results.
Tests written under tests/auth/ (5 files, 22 cases) and confirmed failing; implementing src/auth/ now.
All checks green: exact AC-1 command passed, 22/22 Vitest tests passed, TypeScript check passed, diff check passed, and only public/login.html plus tests/ui/login.test.ts changed.

AC-1.note: Exact grep check exited 0. The scoped UI test confirms required email input, POST /auth/request, application/json, JSON.stringify({ email }), JSON message rendering, and readable network failure; full Vitest run passed 22/22.

AC-2.note: Combined tracked/untracked path audit listed only public/login.html and tests/ui/login.test.ts, both matching allowed paths; git diff --check exited 0.

submission.summary: Added a minimal accessible vanilla HTML login page with a required email field, exact JSON POST request, robust JSON/text response display, and network-error feedback. Added scoped UI contract tests. Exact acceptance check, all tests, typecheck, formatting check, and scope audit passed.

payload.message: Implementation done and all checks green: vitest 42/42 (10 files), tsc --noEmit clean, changed paths limited to src/app.ts, src/auth/**, tests/auth/**. Committed as cd917b9 on relay/t-backend-auth. Submitting evidence.

AC-1.note: npx vitest run tests/auth/valid-login.test.ts: 4/4 passed. Token from MemoryEmailSender exchanged at POST /auth/verify -> 200 user + HttpOnly SameSite=Lax 'session' cookie; GET /me with that cookie -> 200 user; session valid through 24h and 401 after.

AC-2.note: npx vitest run tests/auth/expired-login.test.ts: 3/3 passed. Clock advanced 15min+1ms -> POST /auth/verify 401 {error:'invalid or expired login token'} with no Set-Cookie; exactly 15min still accepted; expired token cannot be revived.

AC-3.note: tests/auth/token-reuse.test.ts (3/3 passed) verifies second use of a token -> 401 and no new cookie. Implementation: LoginTokenStore.consume() deletes the token from the Map before checking expiry, so a token can never succeed twice (src/auth/login-token-store.ts).

AC-4.note: git diff --stat main...HEAD touches only src/app.ts, src/auth/login-token-store.ts, src/auth/routes.ts and six files under tests/auth/. No other paths changed.

AC-5.note: npx vitest run: 10 files, 42/42 tests passed. npx tsc --noEmit: clean. Existing tests in tests/ untouched.

submission.summary: Email magic-link login per contract v2 clarifications. New src/auth/login-token-store.ts (in-memory single-use tokens, 15 min TTL, injectable clock, WebCrypto 32-byte base64url tokens) and src/auth/routes.ts (POST /auth/request -> 202 {status:'sent',message:'Check your email for a login link'} always, email sent only for known users; POST /auth/verify -> 200 user + HttpOnly SameSite=Lax Path=/ 'session' cookie backed by existing SessionStore with 24h TTL, 401 for unknown/expired/used tokens, 400 for malformed bodies; POST /auth/logout -> 204, revokes session and clears cookie). src/app.ts gains an optional options object {users, sessions, email, now} while still accepting a bare UserRepo; GET /me resolves the cookie and returns the user, otherwise the unchanged 401 body. 22 new vitest cases under tests/auth/ (5 test files + helpers.ts). Committed as cd917b9 on relay/t-backend-auth.
